photo.title: Brihadishwara Temple, Dedicated to Shiva, built by Rajaraja I, completed in 1010, Thanjavur (38)
photo.author: Richard Mortel
photo.modifications: cropped to four lines of the inscription, resized and re-encoded (AVIF, WebP, JPEG)
photo.era_en: Chola period (the temple was completed in 1010 CE under Rajaraja I)
photo.era_ta: சோழர் காலம் (கோயில் கி.பி. 1010-இல் முதலாம் இராசராசன் காலத்தில் நிறைவுற்றது)

boxes_method: Hand-annotated on 2x zooms with a pixel grid, guided by a groove-detection pass (local-darkness threshold + connected components). One box per carved letter group (a consonant with its attached vowel signs). Verified by rendering design/hero/boxes-overlay.jpg.

glyphs.method: Reader.read_glyphs: per row, the clean crop and the crop with numbered boxes (design/hero/boxes.json) in one vision call; the model names the modern Tamil letter in each box with its probability that the letter is right

The hero shows this letter-by-letter reading: for each hand-drawn box, the modern Tamil letter the Reader named and its own probability that the letter is right (self-reported, not calibrated). Letters it named under 0.5 were treated as gaps and sent to the Restorer.

restore.note: Candidate fills from the LLM were ranked by the hosted Strands Decider (restorer.strategy_llm: noul-topk, top 3). Without a calibration for that decider the Restorer fills only at confidence >= 0.5; the best fill scored under that, so the gap is left open.

line_reading.note: The app's own line-by-line reading of the same crop (Sonnet 4.6, then Opus 4.6 on 'read again'), and the Restorer on its gaps. Kept for the record; the hero shows the letter-by-letter reading.

edition_note: This stone is not identified in DHARMA or another published edition we could find, so the hero shows no edition text, no match rate and no translation. A search of Wikimedia Commons for an openly licensed photo of an inscription in the DHARMA split found none whose text could be matched to an edition (2026-11-02).

live_calls.note: Bedrock calls. Reader: includes a Sonnet+Opus read of a 6-line crop of the same photo that was not used. Glyphs: one Opus call per row. Restorer: 6 on the line reading (two runs) and 1 on the letter-by-letter reading. Strands Decider calls go to the hosted decider API, not Bedrock.
